title: Novice First PC Build
task: installing CPU and AIO cooler on a first PC build
setting: Home-office desk draped in a red towel holds a Gigabyte Z390 board, Intel LGA1151 CPU, Corsair 280mm AIO with ML140 fans, loose screws, manuals and bags; a gray mid-tower case and component boxes sit nearby under head-cam POV.

steps.text: Seat the CPU in the motherboard socket
steps.detail: Bare hands lift the CPU from its clamshell, lower it into the open socket on the towel-mounted board, nudge it flat, and work the retention hardware.
flags: fingers on the CPU heat spreader
pressing the CPU by hand instead of letting the load plate seat it
steps.expected: ESD strap must be worn and board must rest on anti-static mat; CPU handled by edges only and seated solely by closing the load plate—manual pressing and bare-hand contact with IHS are incorrect

steps.text: Fit the AIO backplate behind the socket
steps.detail: Hands hold the Intel X-mount bracket and leaflet, then flip the board face-down onto the towel and seat the backplate over the socket holes beside a Corsair fan.
flags: board flipped components-down onto the towel
steps.expected: Backplate may be fitted after CPU install but motherboard must stay supported component-side up or on proper standoffs; flipping components-down onto fabric towel risks damage and is incorrect

steps.text: Bring the open case and AIO to the bench
steps.detail: Hands carry the radiator-and-pump assembly across to the open gray mid-tower case among the component boxes.
steps.expected: Case and radiator may be brought over only after pump block is fully mounted to CPU; moving the AIO assembly earlier is out of order

steps.text: Connect the fan leads and screw both fans to the radiator
steps.detail: Hands join the keyed fan-lead connectors above the 280mm radiator, then drive screws to mount both white Corsair ML140 fans onto it.
flags: screws left loose on the towel
steps.expected: Fans can be attached to radiator at this stage provided screws are driven fully and spare hardware is kept organized—not left loose on the towel

steps.text: Orient the pump block and tubes
steps.detail: Hands grip the sleeved tubes and pump block against the case edge, turning the assembly to settle the mounting orientation.
steps.expected: Pump/tube orientation is set only after brackets are on the block and immediately before securing it to the CPU; handling the loose assembly now is premature

steps.detail: A hand digs through a drawer of cable bins while the finished rad-and-fan assembly rests on the towel amid loose leads.
flags: cables left tangled across the workspace
steps.expected: Cable management occurs after all hardware is mounted; rummaging and leaving leads tangled mid-build is out of order and poor practice

steps.text: Test-fit the AIO radiator into the case top
steps.detail: One hand hoists the case and its vented top frame overhead while the other dangles the pump by its tubes, aligning the radiator with the top mount.
steps.expected: Radiator test-fit/install happens only after motherboard is in the case and pump is mounted; pump must never dangle by its tubes and case must remain stable on the desk—not held overhead one-handed

afterClip: Mount the radiator into the case top with the fans screwed through the tray, bolt the pump block onto the CPU using the X bracket over the pre-applied paste, then install the motherboard in the case, add RAM, GPU, and PSU, and connect front-panel, fan, and pump headers before first boot.
procedure: Set up ESD-safe workspace with grounded wrist strap and anti-static mat (never fabric)
Open LGA1151 socket, handle CPU by edges only, align notches and lower gently into socket without touching contacts or IHS pads
Close load plate so it seats the CPU; never press CPU by hand
Apply correct amount of thermal paste if AIO cold-plate lacks pre-applied paste
Install AIO backplate on rear of motherboard while board is supported component-side up or on standoffs
Attach Intel mounting brackets to pump block per Corsair instructions
Place pump block on CPU and tighten mounting screws in cross pattern to even pressure
Install motherboard into case and secure all standoffs/screws
Mount ML140 fans to radiator with correct airflow direction and fully tighten screws, keeping hardware organized
Mount radiator to case top (or chosen location) only after motherboard and pump are installed; never let pump hang by tubes
Connect pump to AIO/CPU_PUMP header and fans to fan headers
Route tubes without kinks or strain and tidy all cables
